content: The development and implementation of systems, including newly created ones, should aim to progressively reduce the amount of effort required for their operation. Steps 5 to 7 focus on the annual collection, monitoring, dissemination, and improvement of Human Resources for Health (HRH) data, as well as the development of new data sources and providers. However, the inclusion of additional stakeholders or changes in ministerial support and national governance structures can influence the long-term sustainability of the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA). Phase III: Scaling Up and Sustainability The objectives of this phase include understanding the successes and failures of the initial NHWA process by reviewing Steps 1 to 7. This review should encompass governance, the legal environment, data gaps and flow, the analysis plan, and the communication plan. Based on lessons learned from previous HRH evaluations, preparations should be made for the next round of data collection, including identifying new data sources if necessary. Key Outputs 1. The NHWA implementation framework should be revised to incorporate experiences gained and any necessary changes in stakeholder participation. 2. A plan should be developed by the multi-stakeholder working group to generate the health workforce data required to meet health policy needs. 3. Existing core indicators should be reviewed, with outdated or irrelevant indicators removed or replaced, and new NHWA indicators added as needed. Additional stakeholders should be identified as potential responsible entities for these new indicators. 4. An annual review meeting should be held to update the composition and terms of reference of the working group. During this meeting, members should evaluate the governance structure, approve necessary amendments, confirm or update focal points, and identify new stakeholders to provide data or assume responsibilities at the national level. 5. The secretariat should present an overview of successes and failures from the previous NHWA implementation round, along with proposals for improving the framework. 6. Additional catalytic funds may be mobilized to produce indicators beyond the core set gathered in the previous round. References The implementation of NHWA is supported by various global strategies and frameworks, including the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (WHO, 2016), resolutions from the World Health Assembly, and contributions from the High-Level Commission on Health Employment and Economic Growth. Additional resources include comprehensive health labor market frameworks, NHWA handbooks, and reports from regional workshops. Best practices in data quality and statistical frameworks from organizations such as the United Nations, FAO, and Statistics Canada also provide valuable guidance for ensuring robust and evidence-based policy decisions.
